$comment: F5.5 — the machine-readable half of the Foundation gate.
One list, read by two tools that must not disagree: scripts/verify.mjs resolves the pipeline
stages whose commands are owned by another phase, and scripts/certify-foundation.mjs decides
whether the evidence a phase promised actually exists on disk. Two hand-maintained copies of
this list would drift, and the copy that drifts is always the one the certification reads.
`anyOf` means the exact filename is not yet settled by the owning agent; the first path that
exists satisfies the entry. An entry with no present path is BLOCKED — never assumed green,
never dropped from the plan. `command` is what the pipeline runs once the evidence exists.
This file records what each phase MUST produce. It does not record that any of it passed.
The checkbox in docs/development/infrastructure-foundation-todolist.md remains the only place
a phase is declared closed, and only the orchestrator writes there.

F3.title: Data, backup and the PostgreSQL migration path
F3.handoffNote: F3.1-F3.5 were executed by the orchestrator directly rather than by a dev1 agent, so there is no _workspace handoff. The evidence — commands, exit codes, negative proofs and residual risks — is in the phase report itself, which is the durable record rather than session scratch.

evidence.description: Portable backup runner a future scheduler can call (F3.5).
Retention selector — it decides which backups get deleted (F3.3).
Month and ISO-week arithmetic of the retention selector.
Backup/PITR staleness alarm (F3.4).
Point-in-time restore into an isolated instance, RPO/RTO measured (F3.4).
Encrypted dump/restore round trip, run on every backend build.

F4.title: Observability, security and software supply chain
F4.handoffNote: F4.1-F4.5 were executed by the orchestrator directly rather than by a dev2 agent. Same reasoning as F3: the phase report is the record, and it also carries the F4 phase-gate section explaining which scanners could not run here.

evidence.description: F4.1 — a local collector receives a correlated trace, metric and log from API and worker.
F4.2 — a payload deliberately full of secret-shaped values must not reach any log or export.
F4.3 — the metric/alert contract, with thresholds left in configuration. Landed as alerting.md; the speculative names are kept so the entry still resolves either way.
F4.4 — dependency audit, secret scan, SAST and image scan, each failing on a deliberate fixture.
F4.4 — weekly npm, NuGet, Docker and GitHub Actions updates.
F4.4 — High/Critical findings are exempted only with a reason, an owner and an expiry.
F4.5 — SBOM, provenance and a keyless Cosign signature bound to an immutable image digest.

F5.title: Unified CI and Foundation Ready certification

evidence.description: F5.1 — the single ordered verification command.
F5.1 — no test is skipped without a dated, owned exemption.
F5.1 — generated artifacts are reproducible and untracked.
F5.2 — Linux runs the whole pipeline; Windows runs the portability gates.
F5.3 — the idempotency suite, ten consecutive iterations, no workflow-level retry.
F5.4 — every fault drill, each with the failure it is required to produce.
F5.5 — collects every phase's evidence and refuses to certify an incomplete one.
Elapsed-time record, separating filesystem-derived span from proven continuous execution.
